$comment: Lincoln's ordinance is carried as NOT in effect (blocked by court order). Omaha's took effect 2026-10-01 after a Douglas County judge enjoined only its youth/training-wage provisions on 2026-09-28; its adult rate is $15.00, the same as the state's, so nothing changes in what an Omaha employer owes until the 2027-01-01 cost-of-living step. LB 258 (2026) created a $13.50 youth and training wage below the state's $15.00 and both cities legislated to undo that locally; the state sued.

jurisdictions.name: Omaha
jurisdictions.coverage: Ordinance No. 44716 (Omaha Municipal Code ch. 39): $15.00 for hours worked in Omaha, rising each 2027-01-01 by the Midwest CPI-U increase (rounded up to the next 5 cents), published by the city by each October 15. Its removal of the state's youth and training wage is ENJOINED: employers qualifying under Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1203(5) and 48-1203.01 may still pay $13.50 to non-emancipated 14-15 year olds and to 16-19 year old new hires for their first 90 days. The engine has no employee-age input, so those $13.50 figures are not computed here.
jurisdictions.note: IN EFFECT from 2026-10-01 for the general rate. Douglas County District Court (Judge Burns, CI 26-7306, order dated 2026-09-28) granted the State a temporary injunction only as to the youth/training-wage provisions and denied it as to the rest, including the faster cost-of-living increase starting 2027-01-01. The adult rate equals the state's $15.00 through 2026, so the binding figure is unchanged. The 2027 amount is deliberately not guessed: the city publishes it by 2026-10-15, and the Attorney General has said he expects further filings on the growth rate. A temporary injunction is not a final order -- re-verify before 2027-01-01.

sources.title: Order on Plaintiff's Motion for Temporary Injunction, State ex rel. Hilgers v. City of Omaha, CI 26-7306 (Douglas County District Court, 2026-09-28)
sources.verifiedBy: PRIMARY: the court's order read in full this session (via a remote fetcher; the filing as hosted by the Nebraska Examiner). It states the ordinance's effective date of 2026-10-01, enjoins only the removal of the youth and training wage, and denies the injunction as to the general minimum wage and its annual increase.

jurisdictions.name: Lincoln
jurisdictions.coverage: Ordinance No. 21872 would have restored a uniform $15.00 and a CPI-U escalator effective 2026-07-18.
jurisdictions.note: NOT IN EFFECT. A Lancaster County District Court judge blocked Lincoln from enacting the ordinance on 2026-07-17, the day before it would have taken effect. Nebraska's state figures apply in Lincoln.

knownGaps: Omaha's youth/training-wage carve-out is enjoined, not struck down: the order is a temporary injunction in a case at its initial stage and can change. The engine has no employee-age input, so the $13.50 youth and training figures are described here but not computed.
Omaha's 2027-01-01 cost-of-living figure is not yet published (due from the city by 2026-10-15) and is not guessed. The State disputes the faster growth rate and expects further filings.
Lincoln's ordinance is carried as blocked on the strength of news coverage; the Lancaster County order itself was not read.
